reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes an atmospheric-pressure plasma jet for oxidation, not plasma immersion ion implantation with nitrogen on TiB₂. It provides no support for nitride layer formation on borides, reduced reactivity with molten aluminum, or the specific process conditions claimed.
premises: PIII with nitrogen can form a continuous nitride-rich surface layer on TiB₂
The nitride layer reduces chemical interaction with molten aluminum
The process can be performed at ~700°C to facilitate surface nitriding
Nitride phases (e.g., BN-like or TiN) have lower chemical affinity for aluminum
